detail: supported
The method operates by blending training images together to render novel views [S1].

The claim states that the method operates by blending training images together to render novel views. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the passages section, stating: 'SVS requires multiple large CNNs and access to all training images (because it operates by blending training images together) to render novel views.' Additionally, the notes section reiterates: 'A view synthesis method that blends training images together...'
supported
Stable View Synthesis (SVS) is a view synthesis method that blends training images together to render novel views, relying on proxy geometry from an external system [S1].

The claim states that Stable View Synthesis (SVS) blends training images together, relies on proxy geometry from an external system, and is a view synthesis method. Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: it describes SVS as operating by 'blending training images together', relying on 'proxy geometry produced by an external system' (specifically COLMAP), and identifies it as a view synthesis method. The notes also corroborate these details.
supported

It is better suited to large piecewise planar objects (e.g., vehicles) due to its reliance on piecewise planar mesh proxy geometry, whereas it performs poorly on scenes with natural content (trees, grass, flowers) [S1].

The claim is directly supported by the text in Source [S1]. The passage explicitly states: 'We speculate that SVS may be better-suited to large piecewise planar objects (which makes sense, given SVS's reliance on a proxy geometry that is itself a piecewise planar mesh) while ours may be better suited to scenes that contain natural content (trees, grass, flowers, etc).' This aligns perfectly with the claim's assertion that the method (SVS) is better suited for large piecewise planar objects like vehicles due to its reliance on piecewise planar mesh proxy geometry, and performs poorly (or is less suited) on scenes with natural content.
supported
SVS requires multiple large CNNs and access to all training images to render novel views [S1].

The claim states that SVS requires multiple large CNNs and access to all training images to render novel views. supported

*   **Inputs:** A set of training images; proxy geometry produced by an external system [S1].

The claim states that the method uses a set of training images and proxy geometry produced by an external system. The evidence explicitly confirms both points: it mentions that SVS 'relies on a proxy geometry produced by an external system' and that it 'requires... access to all training images' because it 'operates by blending training images together'.
supported
Obtain proxy geometry from an external system [S1].

The claim states that the method obtains proxy geometry from an external system. The evidence explicitly states in Source [S1] passages that 'SVS relies on a proxy geometry produced by an external system' and mentions that the depth map is produced by 'COLMAP [45] which is used by SVS'. Additionally, the notes confirm that the method relies on 'proxy geometry from an external system'. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
supported
It struggles particularly with distant or unobserved content, such as trees, where the proxy geometry reconstruction (e.g., via COLMAP) is poor [S1].

The claim states that the method (SVS) struggles with distant or unobserved content like trees because the proxy geometry reconstruction (via COLMAP) is poor. The evidence explicitly supports this in two places: 1) The notes state SVS 'may fail when the external proxy geometry is incorrect, particularly struggling with distant/unobserved content like trees.' 2) The passage from Section E states, 'The poor reconstruction quality of COLMAP in the distant trees may explain why SVS struggles with this scene.' Both sources confirm that the struggle with trees is attributed to poor COLMAP reconstruction.
supported
SVS may fail when the external proxy geometry is incorrect [S1].

The claim is explicitly stated in the provided evidence. Source [S1] notes mention that the method 'May fail when the external proxy geometry is incorrect,' and the passages reiterate this by stating 'SVS relies on a proxy geometry produced by an external system (and may fail when that geometry is incorrect).' Additionally, the text explains that SVS struggles with distant/unobserved content like trees due to poor reconstruction quality in those areas by the external system (COLMAP).
supported

It is distinguished from its siblings by its explicit dependence on external proxy geometry (typically piecewise planar meshes) and access to all training images, whereas [High-Frequency Aware Loss](7589-high-frequency-aware-loss.md) and [WD-Regularized Loss](15613-wd-regularized-loss.md) operate within different optimization frameworks without this specific blending-and-proxy requirement [S1].

The claim states that the subject method is distinguished by its explicit dependence on external proxy geometry (typically piecewise planar meshes) and access to all training images, whereas the cited losses operate in different frameworks without this requirement. Source [S1] explicitly confirms that SVS (the subject method) 'relies on a proxy geometry produced by an external system' and 'requires multiple large CNNs and access to all training images'. It also notes that SVS's reliance on 'piecewise planar mesh' proxy geometry makes it better suited for vehicles, while the proposed model does not use proxy geometry. The claim accurately reflects these distinctions found in the evidence.
supported
